title: Algorithmic Bias, Generalist Models, and Clinical Medicine
benchmark_measurement: The paper cites studies measuring stereotype associations and semantic biases related to religious groups. Specifically, it mentions an example where a model's tendency to complete prompts about Muslims with violent imagery was evaluated.
findings: The paper finds that large language models can exhibit harmful stereotype associations against religious groups. It cites a study where GPT-3 completed prompts about Muslims with violent phraseology. It also discusses the concept of 'semantic haze,' arguing that models may have a coarser understanding of less-represented cultural topics, such as Islamic marriage customs, potentially leading to lower-quality information and suboptimal performance in clinical applications like chatbots.
